newsitem.title: CHINA: HK gold ends up on shortcovering, Europe buying.
newsitem.headline: HK gold ends up on shortcovering, Europe buying.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended higher on Wednesday compared to New York's previous close on shortcovering and overseas buying in afternoon trade, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$319.50/320.00 on Wednesday compared to New York's previous close at US$318.00/50 on Tuesday.
Sentiment remained mostly bearish, with some sales from Australia in the early session combined with shortcovering in a mixed market, dealers said.
European buying later in the day boosted prices although gold was seen stuck in a range, traders said.
Gold's downside was pegged at $315 per ounce, while the upside was seen at around $323 per ounce.
The traded range was limited to between $317 and $319 per ounce, dealers said.
Physical demand had perked up as gold prices halted their downward spiral and the physical market was tight following the rush in demand, sources said.
Local tael gold ended HK$8 up at HK$2,965 per tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to +3.00 from its previous fix at nil.
